purpose: Test whether the large NGC6946 residual is primarily a sky-projection orientation error by replacing the image-only position angle with one formula-independent first-harmonic kinematic phase, without fitting speed amplitude or any gravity parameter.

diagnostic.phaseEstimator: gas-and-inverse-variance-weighted least squares of systemic-subtracted observed velocity on cos(theta) and sin(theta) over the unchanged P0746 score mask
diagnostic.formulaPredictions: unchanged fixed Newtonian and simple-MOND circular-speed maps
diagnostic.comparison: rescore registered-baryon and fake-twin predictions using the unit kinematic phase only

claimBoundary: P0747 is explicitly post-reveal and cannot replace the frozen P0746 validation score.
The kinematic axis is a shared observation-geometry nuisance used identically for every gravity formula; it is not a per-formula fit.
No velocity amplitude, inclination, mass-to-light ratio, gravity constant, MOND scale, or dark halo is fitted.
If both formulas improve similarly, the original residual contained projection error; their remaining difference still tests their predicted speed amplitudes.
